ai.summary: One backend API pod in the ecommerce namespace is crash looping because its ConfigMap contains an invalid APP_MODE value, while the rest of the cluster appears healthy.

issues_for_namespace.title: Backend API crash loop due to invalid APP_MODE in ConfigMap
issues_for_namespace.root_cause: The ConfigMap backend-config sets APP_MODE to 'prodution' (a typo for 'production'), which the backend-api application rejects at startup, causing exit code 1 and CrashLoopBackOff.
issues_for_namespace.explanation: The previous container log for backend-api-85db55fcd-c9rhr contains a FATAL line stating APP_MODE='prodution' is invalid and must be 'development' or 'production'. The pod is in CrashLoopBackOff with 3 restarts and last_exit_code 1, matching a startup failure. The readiness probe connection-refused warning is a symptom: the app crashes before it can bind port 8080.
evidence: Log line: FATAL: invalid configuration APP_MODE='prodution' (from ConfigMap backend-config); expected 'development' or 'production'

issues_for_namespace.fix: Change APP_MODE from 'prodution' to 'production' in ConfigMap/ecommerce/backend-config, then restart the backend-api deployment so new pods load the corrected configuration.
kubectl_commands: kubectl get configmap -n ecommerce backend-config -o yaml
kubectl patch configmap -n ecommerce backend-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"APP_MODE":"production"}}'
issues_for_namespace.prevention: Add a CI validation step that rejects any ConfigMap where APP_MODE is not one of the application's accepted values (development, production) before it is applied to the cluster.
confidence_reasons: The log line explicitly names the bad value, its source ConfigMap, and the expected values; the pod crash state and exit code 1 corroborate a startup configuration rejection.
